target: Para penumpang dimohon segera naik ke pesawat melalui pintu tiga.
english: Passengers are requested to board the plane immediately through gate three.
grammar: Announcement style: dimohon = 'are requested to' — in speech you'd just hear tolong or harap.

target: Kereta menuju Bandung akan segera berangkat dari jalur dua.
english: The train to Bandung will depart shortly from track two.
grammar: Station style: menuju = formal 'bound for' — in conversation people just say ke Bandung.

target: Pesawat tujuan Surabaya mengalami keterlambatan sekitar tiga puluh menit.
english: The flight to Surabaya is experiencing a delay of about thirty minutes.
grammar: Announcement verb: mengalami keterlambatan = 'is delayed' — spoken: pesawatnya telat.

target: Mohon perhatian, pintu kereta akan segera ditutup.
english: Attention please, the train doors will close shortly.
grammar: Mohon perhatian = 'attention please', the standard announcement opener; mohon is a formal 'please'.

target: Para penumpang dimohon tetap duduk sampai pesawat berhenti dengan sempurna.
english: Passengers are requested to remain seated until the plane has stopped completely.
grammar: Cabin formula: berhenti dengan sempurna = 'come to a complete stop' — spoken: benar-benar berhenti.

target: Penumpang kereta dimohon berdiri di belakang garis kuning.
english: Train passengers are requested to stand behind the yellow line.
grammar: Platform announcement register: dimohon berdiri — a friend would simply say tolong berdiri.

target: Kami mohon maaf atas keterlambatan kereta ini.
english: We apologize for the delay of this train.
grammar: Official apology: kami mohon maaf atas ... — spoken: maaf ya, keretanya telat.

target: Pesawat akan segera mendarat, mohon kencangkan sabuk pengaman Anda.
english: The plane will land shortly; please fasten your seatbelt.
grammar: Cabin formula: kencangkan sabuk pengaman = 'fasten your seatbelt'; mohon works like 'please'.

target: Para penumpang tujuan Yogyakarta dipersilakan menuju pintu keberangkatan lima.
english: Passengers bound for Yogyakarta are invited to proceed to departure gate five.
grammar: dipersilakan = formal 'are invited to' — everyday version: silakan ke pintu lima.

target: Harap tidak meninggalkan barang bawaan Anda tanpa pengawasan.
english: Please do not leave your luggage unattended.
grammar: harap = formal 'please' of signs and announcements — softer than dilarang, stiffer than tolong.

target: Kereta terakhir menuju Bogor berangkat pukul sebelas malam.
english: The last train to Bogor departs at eleven at night.
grammar: pukul sebelas = formal clock time in announcements — in conversation everyone says jam sebelas.

target: Penumpang yang membawa anak kecil dipersilakan naik terlebih dahulu.
english: Passengers with small children are invited to board first.
grammar: terlebih dahulu = formal 'first, beforehand' — spoken Indonesian says duluan or lebih dulu.

target: Mohon periksa kembali barang bawaan Anda sebelum turun dari kereta.
english: Please check your belongings again before getting off the train.
grammar: barang bawaan = official 'belongings, luggage' — casually people just say barang or tas.

target: Demi keselamatan bersama, penumpang dilarang bersandar pada pintu.
english: For everyone's safety, passengers are forbidden to lean on the doors.
grammar: demi keselamatan bersama = 'for our shared safety' — a fixed announcement opener.

target: Pesawat dari Denpasar telah mendarat di terminal dua.
english: The plane from Denpasar has landed at terminal two.
grammar: telah = the formal 'sudah' of announcements and news — in speech, always sudah.

target: Perjalanan kereta ini akan memakan waktu sekitar dua jam.
english: This train journey will take about two hours.
grammar: memakan waktu = formal 'to take (time)' — spoken: perjalanannya kira-kira dua jam.

target: Para penumpang dimohon mempersiapkan tiket untuk diperiksa petugas.
english: Passengers are requested to have their tickets ready to be checked by the officer.
grammar: mempersiapkan = formal menyiapkan — announcements love memper- verbs; spoken: siapkan tiketnya.

target: Karena cuaca buruk, semua penerbangan sore ini ditunda.
english: Due to bad weather, all flights this afternoon are postponed.
grammar: Announcement passive: ditunda = 'are postponed' — a staff member would say diundur.

target: Penumpang transit dimohon menunggu di ruang tunggu utama.
english: Transit passengers are requested to wait in the main waiting lounge.
grammar: ruang tunggu = 'waiting lounge' — official signage; in speech: tempat nunggu.

target: Mohon jaga jarak aman dari tepi peron.
english: Please keep a safe distance from the edge of the platform.
grammar: peron = 'platform', a station word; mohon jaga jarak = official 'keep your distance'.

target: Pengumuman ini juga berlaku untuk penumpang kelas ekonomi.
english: This announcement also applies to economy class passengers.
grammar: berlaku = formal 'applies, is valid' — you will see it on tickets, rules and notices everywhere.

target: Para penumpang yang terhormat, selamat datang di Stasiun Gambir.
english: Dear passengers, welcome to Gambir Station.
grammar: yang terhormat = 'esteemed, dear' — the polite address of announcements and letters.

target: Anak-anak harap selalu didampingi oleh orang tua selama perjalanan.
english: Children should always be accompanied by their parents during the journey.
grammar: didampingi = formal 'be accompanied' — spoken: anaknya harus sama orang tuanya.

target: Nomor penerbangan Anda dapat dilihat pada layar informasi.
english: Your flight number can be seen on the information screen.
grammar: In announcements dapat = 'can' — in conversation this is always bisa: bisa dilihat.

target: Kepada seluruh penumpang, kami ucapkan selamat jalan dan terima kasih.
english: To all passengers, we bid you a good journey and thank you.
grammar: kami ucapkan = ceremonial 'we express' — spoken: makasih ya, hati-hati di jalan.

target: Dengan hormat, kami sampaikan jadwal rapat bulan depan.
english: Dear Sir or Madam, we hereby convey next month's meeting schedule.
grammar: Dengan hormat = 'Dear Sir/Madam', the fixed opener of every official Indonesian letter.

target: Bersama surat ini kami lampirkan daftar harga terbaru.
english: With this letter we attach the latest price list.
grammar: bersama surat ini = 'enclosed with this letter' — pure letter language, never spoken.

target: Atas perhatian Bapak, kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: For your attention, Sir, we express our thanks.
grammar: Atas perhatian ... terima kasih = the fixed letter closer, 'thank you for your attention'.

target: Hormat kami, bagian pemasaran PT Maju Bersama.
english: Yours faithfully, the marketing department of PT Maju Bersama.
grammar: Hormat kami = 'yours faithfully' — the letter sign-off from a team or company.

target: Saya menulis surat ini untuk mengajukan permohonan cuti.
english: I am writing this letter to submit a leave request.
grammar: mengajukan permohonan = 'to submit a request' — office language; spoken: minta cuti.

target: Dengan ini saya mengajukan pengunduran diri dari jabatan saya.
english: I hereby submit my resignation from my position.
grammar: dengan ini = 'hereby' — a signal of formal writing; nobody says it out loud.

target: Mohon konfirmasi kehadiran Anda paling lambat hari Jumat.
english: Please confirm your attendance by Friday at the latest.
grammar: paling lambat = 'at the latest' — the deadline phrase of letters and forms.

target: Kami mohon maaf atas kesalahan penulisan pada surat sebelumnya.
english: We apologize for the writing error in the previous letter.
grammar: kesalahan penulisan = 'clerical error', letter-speak — spoken: ada salah ketik.

target: Surat lamaran dan riwayat hidup dapat dikirim melalui email kantor.
english: Application letters and CVs can be sent via the office email.
grammar: riwayat hidup = 'curriculum vitae' — job-application word; people just say CV.

target: Demikian surat ini kami buat, atas kerja samanya kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: Thus we have written this letter; we thank you for your cooperation.
grammar: Demikian ... = 'thus ends this letter', the classic closing line of official letters.

target: Kepada Yang Terhormat Ibu Sari di tempat.
english: To the Honorable Mrs. Sari, at her address.
grammar: di tempat on an envelope = 'at your address' — used when the writer skips the full address.

target: Kami sampaikan bahwa kantor akan tutup selama libur Lebaran.
english: We hereby inform you that the office will be closed during the Lebaran holiday.
grammar: bahwa = 'that' introducing a clause — written style; conversation usually drops it.

target: Mohon hadir tepat waktu karena rapat akan dimulai pukul sembilan.
english: Please be present on time because the meeting will start at nine.
grammar: hadir = formal 'datang' — meeting language; spoken: datang ya, jangan telat.

target: Berdasarkan hasil rapat, kegiatan tahunan akan diadakan bulan Agustus.
english: Based on the meeting results, the annual event will be held in August.
grammar: berdasarkan = 'based on' — report language; spoken: dari hasil rapat.

target: Kami mengharapkan balasan Bapak dalam waktu tujuh hari kerja.
english: We await your reply, Sir, within seven working days.
grammar: hari kerja = 'working days' — the official way offices count deadlines.

target: Perusahaan kami bergerak di bidang jasa pengiriman barang.
english: Our company operates in the field of goods delivery services.
grammar: bergerak di bidang = 'operates in the field of' — company-profile phrase, letters only.

target: Mohon maaf, permintaan Bapak belum dapat kami penuhi saat ini.
english: We are sorry, Sir; we cannot yet fulfill your request at this time.
grammar: belum dapat kami penuhi = the polite refusal of letters; spoken: maaf, belum bisa.

target: Segala biaya perjalanan akan ditanggung oleh pihak perusahaan.
english: All travel costs will be borne by the company.
grammar: pihak = 'party, side' (pihak perusahaan = the company) — contract wording, not speech.

target: Apabila ada pertanyaan, silakan hubungi bagian administrasi kami.
english: If there are any questions, please contact our administration department.
grammar: apabila = formal 'if' — letters and rules; in conversation always kalau.

target: Surat keterangan kerja ini dibuat untuk dipakai sebagaimana mestinya.
english: This employment certificate is issued to be used as appropriate.
grammar: sebagaimana mestinya = 'as it should be used' — boilerplate closing official certificates.

target: Dilarang merokok di seluruh area gedung ini.
english: Smoking is prohibited throughout this building.
grammar: Sign register: dilarang = 'it is prohibited' — spoken: tidak boleh merokok di sini.

target: Harap antre dengan tertib di belakang garis ini.
english: Please queue in an orderly manner behind this line.
grammar: dengan tertib = 'in an orderly way' — sign language; spoken: antre yang rapi ya.

target: Mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya, lift sedang dalam perbaikan.
english: We apologize for the inconvenience; the elevator is under repair.
grammar: ketidaknyamanan = 'inconvenience' — apology-notice word built from tidak nyaman.

target: Dilarang membuang sampah di sungai, pelanggar akan didenda.
english: Throwing trash in the river is forbidden; violators will be fined.
grammar: pelanggar = 'violator', from melanggar (break a rule) — sign and law vocabulary.

target: Isilah formulir ini dengan huruf cetak dan tinta hitam.
english: Fill in this form in block letters and black ink.
grammar: -lah on isilah = polite written command — forms say isilah, people say tolong diisi.

target: Kolom tanda tangan harap diisi oleh pemohon sendiri.
english: The signature field should be filled in by the applicant themselves.
grammar: pemohon = 'the applicant', from memohon — form vocabulary; spoken: yang mengajukan.

target: Lampirkan fotokopi kartu identitas pada formulir pendaftaran Anda.
english: Attach a photocopy of your identity card to your registration form.
grammar: Form verb: lampirkan = 'attach (as an enclosure)' — you meet it on every application.

target: Dilarang berjualan di sepanjang trotoar ini.
english: Selling is prohibited along this sidewalk.
grammar: Street-sign pattern: dilarang + verb = 'no ...-ing'; berjualan = to sell as a trade.

target: Harap tenang, ujian sedang berlangsung di ruangan ini.
english: Please be quiet; an exam is in progress in this room.
grammar: sedang berlangsung = 'is in progress' — notice-board phrase; spoken: lagi ada ujian.

target: Jagalah kebersihan lingkungan demi kesehatan kita bersama.
english: Keep the environment clean for the sake of our shared health.
grammar: demi = 'for the sake of' — slogan word on public signs and campaigns.

target: Pengunjung dilarang membawa makanan dan minuman ke dalam museum.
english: Visitors are forbidden to bring food and drinks into the museum.
grammar: Signs pair formal nouns with dilarang: pengunjung = visitors — spoken: tidak boleh bawa makanan.

target: Area ini khusus untuk pemegang kartu anggota.
english: This area is exclusively for membership card holders.
grammar: pemegang kartu = 'card holder' — peN- turns pegang (hold) into the person who holds.

target: Mohon lepas alas kaki sebelum memasuki musala.
english: Please remove your footwear before entering the prayer room.
grammar: alas kaki = 'footwear', the sign word — everyone actually says sepatu dan sandal.

target: Dilarang parkir di depan pintu darurat ini.
english: Parking is prohibited in front of this emergency door.
grammar: darurat = 'emergency' — pintu darurat, keadaan darurat; a word from signs and news.

target: Kawasan ini bebas asap rokok mulai bulan ini.
english: This area is smoke-free starting this month.
grammar: kawasan = official 'zone, area' — signs say kawasan bebas rokok; spoken: daerah.

target: Simpan barang berharga Anda di dalam loker yang tersedia.
english: Store your valuables in the lockers provided.
grammar: yang tersedia = 'that are provided, available' — notice phrasing; spoken: yang ada.

target: Harap matikan telepon genggam selama pertunjukan berlangsung.
english: Please switch off mobile phones while the performance is in progress.
grammar: telepon genggam = official 'mobile phone' — in real life everyone says HP (ha-pe).

target: Pintu ini hanya untuk keadaan darurat, jangan dibuka sembarangan.
english: This door is only for emergencies; do not open it carelessly.
grammar: keadaan darurat = 'an emergency situation' — keadaan makes nouns sound official.

target: Setiap pengunjung wajib mengenakan masker di dalam rumah sakit.
english: Every visitor is required to wear a mask inside the hospital.
grammar: wajib = 'must (by rule)' — sign word; spoken: harus pakai masker.

target: Dilarang mengambil foto dengan lampu kilat di galeri ini.
english: Taking photos with flash is prohibited in this gallery.
grammar: lampu kilat = 'camera flash', the sign word — everyone just says flash.

target: Tulis nama lengkap Anda sesuai kartu identitas.
english: Write your full name as it appears on your identity card.
grammar: sesuai = 'in accordance with' — form instruction; spoken: sama seperti di KTP.

target: Formulir yang sudah diisi harap diserahkan ke loket satu.
english: Completed forms should be handed in at counter one.
grammar: diserahkan = formal 'be handed over' — counter language; spoken: kasih ke loket satu.

target: Dilarang masuk tanpa izin dari petugas keamanan.
english: No entry without permission from the security officer.
grammar: petugas keamanan = official 'security officer' — everyone actually says satpam.

target: Pakailah tangga darurat apabila terjadi kebakaran.
english: Use the emergency stairs if a fire occurs.
grammar: terjadi = formal 'happens, occurs' — news and signs; spoken: kalau ada kebakaran.

target: Harap tutup kembali pintu pagar setelah Anda lewat.
english: Please close the gate again after you pass through.
grammar: kembali after a verb = 'back, again' in notices: tutup kembali — spoken: tutup lagi.

target: Pemerintah mengumumkan kenaikan harga bahan bakar mulai minggu depan.
english: The government announces a fuel price increase starting next week.
grammar: News style: kenaikan harga = 'a price increase' — spoken: harganya naik.

target: Harga beras di pasar tradisional naik sejak awal bulan ini.
english: The price of rice at traditional markets has risen since the start of this month.
grammar: Headline verbs stand bare: naik = 'has risen' — news drops sudah; add it when speaking.

target: Presiden meresmikan jembatan baru di Kalimantan pagi tadi.
english: The president inaugurated a new bridge in Kalimantan this morning.
grammar: meresmikan = 'to officially open', from resmi (official) — the ceremony verb of news.

target: Hujan deras menyebabkan banjir di beberapa wilayah ibu kota.
english: Heavy rain caused flooding in several areas of the capital.
grammar: wilayah = the news word for 'area, region' — in conversation people say daerah.

target: Warga diminta waspada terhadap cuaca ekstrem minggu ini.
english: Residents are asked to be alert to extreme weather this week.
grammar: News passive diminta = '(people) are asked to' — spoken: tolong hati-hati ya.

target: Jumlah wisatawan asing meningkat tajam pada liburan tahun baru.
english: The number of foreign tourists rose sharply during the New Year holidays.
grammar: meningkat = news 'to increase' — spoken: naik; meningkat tajam = rose sharply.

target: Polisi menangkap dua pelaku pencurian sepeda motor semalam.
english: Police arrested two motorcycle theft perpetrators last night.
grammar: pelaku = 'perpetrator' (from laku, act) — crime-news vocabulary; spoken: pencurinya.

target: Sekolah di daerah banjir diliburkan selama tiga hari.
english: Schools in the flooded area are closed for three days.
grammar: diliburkan = 'are given days off', official passive — spoken: sekolahnya libur.

target: Menteri kesehatan mengunjungi rumah sakit umum di Medan kemarin.
english: The health minister visited the public hospital in Medan yesterday.
grammar: rumah sakit umum = 'public hospital' — umum marks public services in official language.

target: Harga cabai turun setelah panen besar di Jawa Timur.
english: Chili prices fell after a big harvest in East Java.
grammar: Headline word order: topic first — Harga cabai turun; spoken: harga cabainya sudah turun.

target: Pemerintah kota membangun taman baru di pusat kota.
english: The city government is building a new park in the city center.
grammar: pemerintah kota = 'city government' — headlines often shorten it to pemkot.

target: Ribuan orang menghadiri festival budaya di Solo akhir pekan lalu.
english: Thousands of people attended the cultural festival in Solo last weekend.
grammar: akhir pekan = news 'weekend' — in conversation everyone says weekend or Sabtu-Minggu.

target: Jalan utama menuju pelabuhan ditutup karena perbaikan jembatan.
english: The main road to the harbor is closed due to bridge repairs.
grammar: pelabuhan = 'harbor', from labuh — pe-...-an builds place nouns in formal Indonesian.

target: Tim nasional berhasil menang dua kosong atas Malaysia tadi malam.
english: The national team managed to win two-nil over Malaysia last night.
grammar: atas after menang = 'over (an opponent)' — sports-news phrasing; spoken: lawan Malaysia.

target: Bank sentral menurunkan suku bunga untuk mendorong ekonomi.
english: The central bank lowered interest rates to encourage the economy.
grammar: suku bunga = 'interest rate', a finance-news term — bunga alone is flower or interest.

target: Kebakaran hutan kembali muncul di beberapa titik di Sumatera.
english: Forest fires have appeared again at several points in Sumatra.
grammar: kembali before a verb = formal 'again' — news: kembali muncul; speech: muncul lagi.

target: Pemerintah menyiapkan bantuan untuk korban gempa di Sulawesi.
english: The government is preparing aid for earthquake victims in Sulawesi.
grammar: bantuan = 'aid', the noun of bantu (help) — -an turns verbs into things given.

target: Harga tiket pesawat diperkirakan naik menjelang hari raya.
english: Airplane ticket prices are expected to rise ahead of the holiday.
grammar: diperkirakan = 'is expected, estimated' — the forecast verb of news; spoken: kayaknya naik.

target: Kota Bandung menjadi tuan rumah lomba robot tingkat nasional.
english: The city of Bandung is hosting the national-level robot competition.
grammar: tuan rumah = 'host (city, team)', literally 'master of the house' — sports-news idiom.

target: Cuaca panas ekstrem melanda beberapa kota besar di Jawa.
english: Extreme hot weather has struck several big cities in Java.
grammar: melanda = news 'to strike, sweep' (weather, floods) — never for people hitting things.

target: Petani mengeluh karena harga pupuk semakin mahal tahun ini.
english: Farmers complain because fertilizer prices are increasingly expensive this year.
grammar: mengeluh = 'to complain', root keluh — the news standard for quoting unhappy groups.

target: Jumlah penduduk ibu kota mencapai sebelas juta jiwa tahun ini.
english: The capital's population reached eleven million people this year.
grammar: jiwa (soul) counts people in statistics: sebelas juta jiwa = eleven million people.

target: Pameran buku nasional dibuka untuk umum mulai hari Rabu.
english: The national book fair opens to the public starting Wednesday.
grammar: untuk umum = 'for the public' — notice and news phrase; umum also means 'general'.

target: Angka kecelakaan lalu lintas menurun selama bulan puasa.
english: The number of traffic accidents declined during the fasting month.
grammar: angka = 'figure, number' in statistics news: angka kecelakaan = accident numbers.

target: Perusahaan teknologi lokal membuka seribu lapangan kerja baru.
english: A local technology company is opening a thousand new jobs.
grammar: lapangan kerja = 'jobs, employment' (literally 'work field') — economy-news collocation.

target: Kami mengundang Bapak dan Ibu untuk hadir pada acara pernikahan putri kami.
english: We invite you, Sir and Madam, to attend our daughter's wedding ceremony.
grammar: Invitation style: mengundang Bapak/Ibu = formal 'you' — never kamu on an invitation.

target: Acara akan diadakan pada hari Minggu, pukul sepuluh pagi.
english: The event will be held on Sunday at ten in the morning.
grammar: diadakan = 'will be held', invitation passive — spoken: acaranya hari Minggu jam sepuluh.

target: Kami mengharapkan kehadiran Saudara pada rapat warga bulan ini.
english: We look forward to your presence at this month's residents' meeting.
grammar: Saudara = very formal 'you' on invitations and forms — heard almost only in officialese.

target: Acara syukuran akan bertempat di kediaman Bapak Rahmat.
english: The thanksgiving celebration will take place at Mr. Rahmat's residence.
grammar: kediaman = formal 'residence' — invitations say kediaman, everyone else says rumah.

target: Mohon doa restu untuk pernikahan putra kami bulan depan.
english: We ask for your blessing for our son's wedding next month.
grammar: doa restu = 'prayers and blessing' — a fixed wedding-invitation phrase.

target: Atas kehadiran dan doa Bapak Ibu, kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: For your presence and prayers, we express our thanks.
grammar: Invitation closer: atas kehadiran ... terima kasih — thanks given before the event happens.

target: Kami mohon kehadiran Bapak tepat waktu karena acara dimulai sore hari.
english: We request your presence on time because the event begins in the late afternoon.
grammar: mohon kehadiran = 'we request your presence' — spoken this is just: datang ya.

target: Turut mengundang keluarga besar Wijaya dan rekan kantor.
english: Also extending the invitation: the extended Wijaya family and office colleagues.
grammar: Turut mengundang = 'also inviting' — the line listing extra hosts at the bottom of invitations.

target: Kehadiran Bapak dan Ibu akan menjadi kehormatan bagi keluarga kami.
english: Your presence will be an honor for our family.
grammar: bagi = formal 'untuk' (for) — invitation and news word; spoken: untuk keluarga kami.

target: Acara dilanjutkan dengan makan siang bersama di ruang utama.
english: The event continues with a shared lunch in the main hall.
grammar: dilanjutkan dengan = 'followed by' — programme wording on invitations.

target: Kami mengundang seluruh warga untuk mengikuti kerja bakti hari Minggu pagi.
english: We invite all residents to join the community work day on Sunday morning.
grammar: kerja bakti = 'community work day' — a fixed term on neighborhood invitations.

target: Mohon kehadiran Ibu pada pertemuan orang tua murid hari Sabtu.
english: We request your presence, Madam, at the parents' meeting on Saturday.
grammar: pertemuan = formal 'meeting', from bertemu — schools write pertemuan, parents say rapat.

target: Undangan ini berlaku untuk dua orang termasuk anak-anak.
english: This invitation is valid for two people, including children.
grammar: termasuk = 'including' — the ter- form of masuk; common in rules and invitations.

target: Besar harapan kami Bapak dapat hadir dan memberikan sambutan.
english: It is our great hope that you can attend and give a speech.
grammar: Besar harapan kami = 'it is our great hope' — a super-polite invitation formula.

target: Kami menantikan kehadiran Anda sekeluarga pada acara ulang tahun perusahaan.
english: We look forward to the presence of you and your family at the company anniversary event.
grammar: menantikan = 'to look forward to, await' — the formal menunggu; invitations love it.

target: Nasabah dimohon mengambil nomor antrean sebelum menuju loket.
english: Customers are requested to take a queue number before proceeding to the counter.
grammar: nasabah = 'bank customer' — only banks use it; shops say pelanggan or pembeli.

target: Kantor cabang kami buka setiap hari kerja mulai pukul delapan.
english: Our branch office is open every working day from eight o'clock.
grammar: kantor cabang = 'branch office' — cabang is the branch of a tree, a bank, a company.

target: Biaya administrasi sebesar lima ribu rupiah dikenakan untuk setiap transaksi.
english: An administration fee of five thousand rupiah is charged for each transaction.
grammar: sebesar = 'in the amount of' (se- + besar) — money notices use it before every figure.

target: Mesin ATM di lantai satu sedang dalam perbaikan sementara.
english: The ATM on the first floor is temporarily under repair.
grammar: sedang dalam perbaikan = 'under repair', notice formula — spoken: lagi diperbaiki.

target: Mohon jangan memberikan kata sandi Anda kepada siapa pun.
english: Please do not give your password to anyone.
grammar: kata sandi = official 'password' — most Indonesians just say password; sandi = code.

target: Layanan pelanggan kami dapat dihubungi dua puluh empat jam.
english: Our customer service can be reached twenty-four hours a day.
grammar: layanan = formal 'service', from melayani — notices write layanan, speech often servis.

target: Rapat seluruh karyawan akan diadakan hari Jumat pukul dua siang.
english: An all-staff meeting will be held on Friday at two in the afternoon.
grammar: karyawan = 'employee', the office word — casual speech says pegawai or orang kantor.

target: Seluruh karyawan diwajibkan mengikuti pelatihan keselamatan kerja bulan depan.
english: All employees are required to attend the occupational safety training next month.
grammar: diwajibkan = 'are required to', HR passive — spoken: semua harus ikut.

target: Kartu yang tertelan mesin dapat diambil di kantor cabang terdekat.
english: A card swallowed by the machine can be collected at the nearest branch office.
grammar: tertelan = 'accidentally swallowed' — ter- marks accidents: kartunya tertelan mesin.

target: Harap simpan bukti pembayaran ini sebagai tanda terima yang sah.
english: Please keep this proof of payment as a valid receipt.
grammar: sah = 'valid, legal' — stamp-and-signature word: tanda terima yang sah = a valid receipt.

target: Pengambilan uang di atas sepuluh juta harap dilaporkan sehari sebelumnya.
english: Withdrawals above ten million should be reported one day in advance.
grammar: pengambilan uang = 'withdrawal', teller language — spoken: mau ambil uang.

target: Sistem kami akan diperbarui malam ini mulai pukul sebelas.
english: Our system will be updated tonight starting at eleven.
grammar: diperbarui = 'be updated, renewed', from baru (new) — memper- means 'make more X'.

target: Selama jam istirahat, pelayanan di loket dua dihentikan sementara.
english: During the break, service at counter two is temporarily suspended.
grammar: dihentikan sementara = 'temporarily suspended', notice-speak — spoken: loketnya tutup dulu.

target: Mohon maaf, layanan transfer antarbank sedang mengalami gangguan.
english: We apologize; the interbank transfer service is currently experiencing a disruption.
grammar: mengalami gangguan = 'experiencing a disruption', outage-notice formula — spoken: lagi error.

target: Terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda kepada bank kami selama ini.
english: Thank you for your trust in our bank all this time.
grammar: atas after terima kasih = formal 'for': terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda — speech drops atas.
